title:	Change the cursor type from an arrow to a hand when hovering over multiple-month-view calendar icons
state:	OPEN
author:	RaccoonSwarm
labels:	scope: small
comments:	0
assignees:	bennettmatuszewski (Bennett Matuszewski)
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	25
--
### Summary
In the budget section of the app where the monthly budgets are shown, the top left corner has multiple calendar icons to allow users to select how many months are displayed at a time. When you hover over most clickable icons on the app, the cursor changes from an arrow to a hand. Currently, the cursor does not change to a hand over these calendar icons. This makes it harder for the user to know that they can click on these, and it may prevent them from knowing that this functionality exists. Changing the cursor to be a hand when hovering over these buttons would make the user interface more cohesive and could allow for more users to utilize the multiple-month viewing feature. 

### User Story
As a user, I really appreciate consistency in an app's design. I want to see the same pointer cursor when I hover over anything I can click on. The main budget screen has an option to display multiple months at once, but I had no idea I could do that for a long time because it's hard to tell that those icons have that functionality. The cursor stays an arrow when I hover over them and I think it would be really helpful and add more consistency if it changed to the pointer/hand cursor.

### Rough Scope
Small -- This change to the cursor's appearance is relatively simple. You could reuse code from other parts of the project since the same behavior is used when hovering over many other clickable icons. The difficulty would not be in the implementation but instead in finding where to make the change in the code. 

### Source
The issue arose when discussing the UI with a teammate and from my own personal experience.

5	## Project Overview

42	- Use `yarn workspace <workspace-name> run <command>` for workspace-specific tasks
43	- Tests run once and exit by default (using `vitest --run`)

51	
52	The project uses **[lage](https://microsoft.github.io/lage/)** (a task runner for JavaScript monorepos) to efficiently run tests and other tasks across multiple workspaces:
53	
54	- **Parallel execution**: Runs tests in parallel across workspaces for faster feedback
55	- **Smart caching**: Caches test results to skip unchanged packages (cached in `.lage/` directory)
56	- **Dependency awareness**: Understands workspace dependencies and execution order
57	- **Continues on error**: Uses `--continue` flag to run all packages even if one fails

60

63	yarn test                    # Equivalent to: lage test --continue

66	yarn test:debug              # Equivalent to: lage test --no-cache --continue
67	```

266	## Code Style & Conventions
267	
268	### TypeScript Guidelines
269	
270	**Type Usage:**
271	
272	- Use TypeScript for all code; look for existing type definitions before adding new ones
273	- Prefer `satisfies` over type assertions (`as`, `!`) for narrowing
274	
275	**Naming:**
276	
277	- Use descriptive variable names with auxiliary verbs (e.g., `isLoaded`, `hasError`)
278	
279	**Code Structure:**
280	
281	- Functional and declarative programming patterns - avoid classes
282	- Use the `function` keyword for pure functions
283	- Prefer iteration and modularization over code duplication
284	- Structure files: exported component/page, helpers, static content, types
285	- Create new components in their own files
286	
287	**React Patterns:**
288	
289	- The project uses **React Compiler** (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`) in the desktop-client. The compiler auto-memoizes component bodies, so you can omit manual `useCallback`, `useMemo`, and `React.memo` when adding or refactoring code; prefer inline callbacks and values unless a stable identity is required by a non-compiled dependency.
290	- Avoid unstable nested components
291	
292	**JSX Style:**
293	
294	- Declarative JSX, minimal and readable
295	- Avoid unnecessary curly braces in conditionals
296	- Use concise syntax for simple statements
297	- Prefer explicit expressions (`condition && <Component />`)
298	
299	### Platform-Specific Code
300	
301	- Use conditional exports in `loot-core` for platform-specific code; platform
302	  resolution happens at build time via package.json exports. Don't directly
303	  import another platform's modules (`.api`, `.electron`).
304	
305	For commit and PR rules, see
306	[PR and Commit Rules](.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md).
307

438	
439	### Type Errors
440	
441	1. Run `yarn typecheck` to see all type errors

444	4. Use `satisfies` instead of `as` for type narrowing

447	
448	Run `yarn lint` to check. All rules — including the custom `actual/*` rules
449	(`no-untranslated-strings`, `prefer-trans-over-t`, `prefer-logger-over-console`,
450	`typography`, …) — are defined in [`.oxlintrc.json`](.oxlintrc.json).

452	### Test Failures
453	
454	1. Check if test is running in correct environment (node vs web)
455	2. For Vitest: check `vitest.config.ts` or `vitest.web.config.ts`
456	3. For Playwright: check `playwright.config.ts`
457	4. Ensure mock minimization - prefer real implementations

459	6. **Tests continue on error**: With `--continue` flag, all packages run even if one fails

461	### Import Resolution Issues
462	
463	1. Check `tsconfig.json` for path mappings
464	2. Check package.json `exports` field (especially for loot-core)

466	4. Use absolute imports in `desktop-client`

471	2. Reinstall dependencies: `yarn install`
472	3. Check Node.js version (requires >=22)

558	## Cursor Cloud specific instructions
559	
560	### Services overview
561	
562	| Service             | Command                 | Port | Required                      |
563	| ------------------- | ----------------------- | ---- | ----------------------------- |
564	| Web Frontend (Vite) | `yarn start`            | 3001 | Yes                           |
565	| Sync Server         | `yarn start:server-dev` | 5006 | Optional (sync features only) |
566	
567	All storage is **SQLite** (file-based via `better-sqlite3`). No external databases or services are needed.
568	
569	### Running the app
570	
571	- `yarn start` builds the plugins-service worker, loot-core browser backend, and starts the Vite dev server on port **3001**.
572	- `yarn start:server-dev` starts both the sync server (port 5006) and the web frontend together.
573	- The Vite HMR dev server serves many unbundled modules. In constrained environments, the browser may hit `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`. If that happens, use `yarn build:browser` followed by serving the built output from `packages/desktop-client/build/` with proper COOP/COEP headers (`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`).
574	
575	### Lint, test, typecheck
576	
577	Standard commands documented in `package.json` scripts and the Quick Start section above:

591	- Lage caches test results in `.lage/`. If tests behave unexpectedly, clear with `rm -rf .lage`.
592	- Native modules (`better-sqlite3`, `bcrypt`) require build tools (`gcc`, `make`, `python3`). These are pre-installed in the Cloud VM.

# PR and Commit Rules for AI Agents

This file lists the PR and commit rules you have to apply yourself.

## Pull Request Rules

### `[AI]` prefix on PR titles

**ALL pull request titles MUST be prefixed with `[AI]`** — you have to apply it
yourself.

**Examples:**

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation`
- `Fix type error in account validation` (MISSING PREFIX — NOT ALLOWED)

### Do not fill in the PR template

- **NEVER fill in the PR template** (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`). Create
  the PR with that template as the body, unmodified — leave all blank spaces and
  placeholder comments as-is, and leave every checklist box unchecked. The human
  who tested the change fills in the Description, Related issue(s), Testing, and
  Checklist sections.
- **Exception**: if a human **explicitly asks** you to fill it out, do so **in
  Chinese**, using Chinese characters (简体中文) for all content you add.

## GitHub comment, review and issue prefix

**Prefix everything you post to GitHub with the robot emoji 🤖** — pull-request
and issue comments, pull-request reviews (including inline review comments), and
the title and body of issues you create. This keeps agent-authored content
visibly marked. It does **not** change PR titles (still `[AI] …`) or commit
messages (still `[AI] …`).

Write the text normally; just make sure 🤖 is the first character (for issues,
on both the title and the body).

This applies only to comments **you** author — bots like CodeRabbit post under
their own identity and are not affected.

title:	Limit the length of Account names
state:	OPEN
author:	icsasso (Isabella Sasso)
labels:	scope: small

projects:

**Summary**

Actual Budget currently does not enforce a maximum character length on bank account name fields. Users who enter an unusually long account name may encounter an unexpected error at save time — after the fact, with no prior warning — rather than being guided toward a valid input as they type. A reasonable character limit enforced at the input level, paired with a visible character counter that warns users as they approach the cap, would prevent silent failures and bring the field in line with standard form UX expectations.

**User Story**

As a user creating or editing a bank account, I want the account name field to show me how close I am to the character limit as I type so that I don't hit an unexpected error after trying to save a name that is too long.

**Rough Scope**

Small — The fix has two parts: adding a 'maxLength' constraint to the account name input, and rendering a character counter near the field that becomes visually prominent as the user nears the limit. Both are frontend-only changes scoped to the account creation and edit forms. The main decision to align on before opening a PR is what the character maximum should be — this should match any constraint already enforced by the underlying data layer or sync backend, if one exists, so that the UI limit and the real limit are never out of sync. A beginner contributor can tackle this with a straightforward understanding of the relevant form component.

**Source**

Assisted with Claude for issue generation.

# Issue #20: Limit the length of Account names

## Context

GitHub issue [#20](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/issues/20) is assigned to the user (TigerK9). Actual Budget doesn't cap account-name length today, so an overly long name can fail silently at save time instead of guiding the user as they type. The fix is frontend-only, scoped to the account **creation** and **edit/rename** forms: add a `maxLength` constraint and a character counter that becomes visually prominent as the limit approaches.

No backend/schema constraint exists to mirror (`loot-core`'s `accounts.name` field is just `f('string', { required: true })`, no length cap), so the max is a UI-only decision — confirmed with the user as **50 characters**.

## Approach

1. **Add a shared max-length constant + validation** in
   [accountValidation.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/util/accountValidation.ts)
   (currently only checks blank/duplicate names, lines 1–22):
   - Export `ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 50`.
   - Extend `validateAccountName()` to return an error when `name.length > ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`, as a safety-net alongside the native `maxLength` attribute.

2. **Add a small reusable counter component**: new file
   `packages/desktop-client/src/components/common/CharacterCounter.tsx` exporting
   `CharacterCounter({ length, maxLength })`. Renders `length/maxLength` as `Text`,
   switching to a warning color (existing theme token, e.g. `theme.warningText` /
   `theme.errorText` — check `@actual-app/components/theme` for the right token)
   once remaining characters drop below a small threshold (e.g. ≤10 left). Used by
   both modals below to avoid duplicating the prominence logic.

3. **Creation form** —
   [CreateLocalAccountModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/CreateLocalAccountModal.tsx):
   - Add `maxLength={ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH}` to the name `Input` (~lines 97–106); the existing `name` state (already wired via `onChangeValue={setName}`) drives the count.
   - Render `<CharacterCounter length={name.length} maxLength={ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH} />` near the input, alongside the existing `FormError`.

4. **Rename/edit form** — the name is edited inline via `ModalTitle` in
   [Modal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/common/Modal.tsx) (lines 384–480ish), used from
   [AccountMenuModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/AccountMenuModal.tsx)
   (`ModalTitle` usage ~lines 130–134, `onRename` handler ~lines 57–84):
   - Add an optional `maxLength?: number` prop to `ModalTitleProps`; pass it straight through to the underlying `Input`'s native `maxLength` (line ~427).
   - Track live length while editing via the `Input`'s `onChangeValue` (same pattern already used in `CreateLocalAccountModal`), and render `CharacterCounter` under the input only while `isEditing && maxLength` is set — keeps `ModalTitle` generic for its other (non-account) callers, since the counter only appears when a caller opts in via `maxLength`.
   - In `AccountMenuModal.tsx`, pass `maxLength={ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH}` to `ModalTitle`.

5. **Release note**: add `upcoming-release-notes/limit-account-name-length.md` per the repo's release-note convention (short plain-language description, no implementation detail).

## Files touched

- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/util/accountValidation.ts` (edit)
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/common/CharacterCounter.tsx` (new)
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/CreateLocalAccountModal.tsx` (edit)
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/common/Modal.tsx` (edit — `ModalTitle`)
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/AccountMenuModal.tsx` (edit)
- `upcoming-release-notes/limit-account-name-length.md` (new)

## Verification

- `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint:fix` from repo root.
- `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test` for any `accountValidation` unit tests (add one for the new length check if a test file already exists for that util).
- Manual check via `yarn start` (or the demo budget): create an account, type a name past ~40 chars and confirm the counter appears/turns prominent, and typing is blocked at 50; rename an existing account the same way via the account menu.

- Branch name: `fix/issue-20-account-name-length` (repo convention).
- PR title must start with `[AI]`; leave the PR template unmodified/blank.
- Log the AI session under `ai-logs/sprint0/tigerk9/` per repo convention once work is done.

import { Text } from '@actual-app/components/text';
import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';

const WARNING_THRESHOLD = 10;

type CharacterCounterProps = {
  length: number;
  maxLength: number;
};

export function CharacterCounter({ length, maxLength }: CharacterCounterProps) {
  const remaining = maxLength - length;
  const isNearLimit = remaining <= WARNING_THRESHOLD;

  return (
    <Text
      style={{
        fontSize: '0.75em',
        color: isNearLimit ? theme.warningText : theme.pageTextLight,
      }}
    >
      {length}/{maxLength}
    </Text>
  );
}

```

import type { AccountEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import {
  ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH,
  validateAccountName,
} from './accountValidation';

const existingAccounts: AccountEntity[] = [
  { id: 'a1', name: 'Checking' } as AccountEntity,
  { id: 'a2', name: 'Savings' } as AccountEntity,
];

describe('validateAccountName', () => {
  it('returns an error for a blank name', () => {
    expect(validateAccountName('', 'a1', existingAccounts)).not.toBe('');
    expect(validateAccountName('   ', 'a1', existingAccounts)).not.toBe('');
  });

  it('returns an error for a duplicate name on a different account', () => {
    expect(
      validateAccountName('Savings', 'a1', existingAccounts),
    ).not.toBe('');
  });

  it('allows keeping an account\'s own current name', () => {
    expect(validateAccountName('Checking', 'a1', existingAccounts)).toBe('');
  });

  it('allows a name at exactly the max length', () => {
    const name = 'a'.repeat(ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH);
    expect(validateAccountName(name, 'a1', existingAccounts)).toBe('');
  });

  it('returns an error for a name longer than the max length', () => {
    const name = 'a'.repeat(ACCOUNT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH + 1);
    expect(validateAccountName(name, 'a1', existingAccounts)).not.toBe('');
  });

  it('returns a valid, non-duplicate, non-blank name unchanged', () => {
    expect(validateAccountName('New Account', 'a1', existingAccounts)).toBe(
      '',
    );
  });
});

```

import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';

import { CharacterCounter } from './CharacterCounter';

describe('CharacterCounter', () => {
  it('renders the current length and max length', () => {
    render(<CharacterCounter length={12} maxLength={50} />);
    expect(screen.getByText('12/50')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('is not warning-colored while far from the limit', () => {
    render(<CharacterCounter length={10} maxLength={50} />);
    const counter = screen.getByText('10/50');
    expect(counter.style.color).not.toBe('');
    expect(counter).not.toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-warning-text)' });
  });

  it('switches to a warning color near the limit', () => {
    render(<CharacterCounter length={45} maxLength={50} />);
    const counter = screen.getByText('45/50');
    expect(counter).toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-warning-text)' });
  });

  it('treats being exactly at the limit as near the limit', () => {
    render(<CharacterCounter length={50} maxLength={50} />);
    const counter = screen.getByText('50/50');
    expect(counter).toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-warning-text)' });
  });
});

Good question — this isn't something specific to your changes. Those two files (`STUDENTS.md` and your teammate's ai-log) were apparently committed before oxfmt's markdown-table rules were applied to them, so they're permanently "out of sync" with the formatter config. There's no ignore rule for them in `.oxfmtrc.json`, so **any** `yarn lint:fix` run from root — by you, a teammate, or CI — will keep reformatting them until either:

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.


ARGUMENTS: Commit the account-name-length changes for GitHub issue #20 on branch fix/issue-20-account-name-length. Commit message title must start with [AI]. After committing, ask whether to also open the PR (leaving the PR template blank/unmodified, per repo rules) before doing so.
